newsitem.title: KENYA: Zairean troops abandon town ahead of rebel advance.
newsitem.headline: Zairean troops abandon town ahead of rebel advance.

text.p: Zairean soldiers have fled the town of Kasenga after clashes with the local population in support of rebel leader Laurent Kabila but the rebels have not entered the town, a regional military source said on Saturday.

The source, who closely monitors the war between Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) and Zaire's ragged army, said the troops looted and rampaged through Kasenga as they fled an angry population early on Friday.

The source spoke a day after expatriates and local sources in the Shaba capital Lubumbashi told Reuters that Kasenga, a tiny fishing town within 220 km (135 miles) reach of Lubumbashi, had been captured by Kabila's rebels.

"Our latest intelligence is that the rebels have not actually entered Kasenga," the source said. "The Zairean soldiers abandoned the town after being attacked by the local population in support of Kabila."
He added: "The skirmishes were serious and a number of people were injured. The population says it is waiting for Kabila's arrival."

A defence ministry official in Kinshasa denied on Friday that Kasenga had fallen. But the source said the town was now being controlled by civilian defence units awaiting the arrival of Kabila's forces said to be advancing towards Kasenga on the Zambian border.
